No car, no parking. Room: 260 sq ft, queen bed + queen Murphy bed, one bathroom, mini fridge; soft-goods refresh finished March 2026. Ten decade-themed buildings (50s–90s) around Hourglass Lake with giant icons; Classic Hall has check-in, the Everything POP food court and bus stops; three pools (Hippy Dippy is the main one). Preferred rooms (+~$30/night) = 50s/60s/70s near Classic Hall; building 3 (60s) is between the lobby and the Skyliner bridge — request '60s, lake view, upper floor away from the pool'. Downsides: one bathroom, food court only, exterior-corridor noise. Early Entry, free parking, no resort fee.

name: Disney park tickets — Thu/Fri/Sat (3× 3-day from Nov 5, 1× 2-day from Nov 6)
notes: Plan: 3 of us in parks Thu Nov 5, Fri Nov 6 (parade at Epcot), Sat Nov 7 → 3-day base tickets starting Thu; the Friday arrival gets a 2-day ticket starting Fri. Disney direct = $1,961 + 6.5% tax = $2,088. Best routes checked 2026-10-10: Undercover Tourist (~$1,987 incl. tax + $80 DiningDollars; pay with Sapphire Reserve to use the $300 travel credit) or Disney direct paid with 5–10%-off gift cards (Target RedCard / Sam's Club). No public Disney ticket promo covers Nov 5–7. Working Advantage needs a BMS login to price. Older per-adult pricing options (3-day base $528 from Fri, Park Hopper, etc.) kept below for reference. Everyone watching the parade needs an Epcot admission for Fri Nov 6.

options.title: 3-day base ticket, start Fri Nov 6 — $528/adult
options.notes: 4 adults = $2,112 pre-tax ($2,249 with tax). $176/day vs $190–195 for 1-day tickets. One park per day. RECOMMENDED.

options.title: 3-day Park Hopper, start Fri Nov 6 — $623/adult
options.notes: 4 adults = $2,492 pre-tax ($2,654 with tax). Only worth it if you want to split days between parks.

options.title: 2-day base ticket, start Sat Nov 7 — $358/adult
options.notes: 4 adults = $1,432 pre-tax ($1,525 with tax). Budget version — but then the parade day (Fri) needs a separate 1-day Epcot ticket (~$170–190).

options.title: 1-day Epcot ticket, Fri Nov 6 — ~$170–190/adult
options.notes: Magic Kingdom 1-day is $190 on Fri Nov 6; Epcot runs ~$10–20 less. Parade-only option for anyone skipping the other park days.

options.title: 4-day base ticket, start Fri Nov 6 — $672/adult
options.notes: 4 adults = $2,688 pre-tax. Only if Monday has a usable park morning (late flight home).

options.title: Undercover Tourist — 3× 3-day (start Thu Nov 5) + 1× 2-day (start Fri Nov 6) — ~$1,987 incl. tax
options.notes: UT calendar prices for our dates: 3-day $166/day = $498; 2-day $186/day = $372 → $1,866 before tax, ~$1,987 with 6.5% tax (confirm tax handling at checkout). About $100 under Disney direct ($2,088 incl. tax), plus a free $20 DiningDollars credit per ticket (4 × $20 toward Disney/restaurant gift cards). E-tickets link straight into My Disney Experience. Codes as TRAVEL on Chase Sapphire Reserve → can burn the $300 annual travel credit if unused, and earns travel points.

options.title: Disney direct, paid with discounted gift cards — ~$1,984 (5% off) / ~$1,880 (10% promo)
options.location: disneyworld.com + Target RedCard / Sam's Club gift cards
options.notes: Disney price for our plan: 3 × 3-day from Thu Nov 5 ($532) + 1 × 2-day from Fri Nov 6 ($365) = $1,961 + 6.5% tax = $2,088. Buy Disney gift cards first: Target RedCard = automatic 5% off (→ ~$1,984); Sam's Club usually $190 per $200 (5%) with occasional 10% promos (→ ~$1,880, limits of ~2 per order); Costco/BJ's run similar deals. Gift cards can't be used at Undercover Tourist, so this is EITHER/OR with the reseller route.

options.title: Working Advantage (BMS employee perks) — log in to price; marketed as 'adult tickets at child prices on 3+ day'
options.notes: Public offer page currently says 'offer not available' and prices are only visible logged in. If the adult-at-child-price deal is live, that's $5–18 off per 3-day ticket (child 3-day for Nov 5 start is ~$514 vs $532) — i.e. LESS than Undercover Tourist unless WA also discounts the child price. Worth a 5-minute login check; TicketsAtWork is the other employer-perk vendor (voucher pickup at the park, slower).

options.title: Chase Sapphire — Ultimate Rewards via Chase Travel 'Activities' (~1¢/point) — NOT recommended for tickets
options.notes: Disney tickets appear intermittently under Activities in Chase Travel and redeem at roughly 1 cent per point (a 1-day ticket was 18,587 pts ≈ 0.9¢). Points are worth more on flights/hotels. Better Sapphire plays: (1) pay Undercover Tourist with the Reserve to use the $300 travel credit, (2) check Chase Offers in the app for an Undercover Tourist / Disney cashback offer, (3) no Disney ticket discount exists for Sapphire; the Disney Visa only gives 10% merch/dining and 0% financing.

options.title: Disney official promos for Nov 5–7 — none apply (reference)
options.notes: Checked 2026-10-10: 4-Park Magic ($99/day) ended with October; Disney+ Perks 3-park ticket deal covered Jan 12–May 22 only; Florida-resident Discover ticket ended Oct 3; 2-Park Explorer ended Sep 30. Only military Salute tickets run through Dec 18. Watch Disney Tourist Blog for a new late-fall ticket offer before booking.

name: Disney park tickets — Thu/Fri (3× 2-day from Nov 5, 1× 1-day EPCOT Fri)
notes: Two park days: Thursday (Magic Kingdom or Hollywood Studios) and Friday (EPCOT, parade). Three of us need a 2-day base ticket starting Thu Nov 5; the Friday arrival needs a 1-day EPCOT ticket. Disney's calendar (Oct 10) shows the 2-day base at $365 for a Fri start and $358 for a Sat start, so a Thu start should land about $360–370 per adult; 1-day EPCOT Friday ~$170–190. Tax 6.5%. The Park Hopper is the only way to add Hollywood Studios on this plan.

options.title: Disney direct — 3× 2-day base (start Thu Nov 5) + 1× 1-day EPCOT (Fri Nov 6) — ~$1,365 incl. tax
options.notes: 3 × ~$365 + ~$180 = ~$1,275 before tax, ~$1,365 with 6.5%. Estimate until the Thursday-start price is read off Disney's calendar. One park per day; a 2-day ticket is valid over a 4-day window so Thu/Fri is covered.

options.title: Disney direct — same mix with Park Hopper on the three 2-day tickets — ~$1,660 incl. tax
options.notes: Adds ~$85–95 per 2-day ticket. Buys Hollywood Studios on Friday evening (Skyliner from EPCOT's International Gateway, ~15 min; Rise of the Resistance needs a Single Pass) or a split Thursday. Skip if the ballot picks one Thursday park and everyone is content with it.

options.title: Disney direct, paid with discounted gift cards — ~$1,297 (5% off) / ~$1,229 (10% promo)
options.notes: Buy ~$1,400 of Disney gift cards first (Target RedCard 5% automatic; Sam's Club / Costco / BJ's $200 cards for $190, sometimes 10%). Same route as the Family Plan's ticket card.

options.title: Undercover Tourist — same mix — ~$1,388 incl. tax + 4 × $20 DiningDollars
options.notes: UT's 2-day ran $7 ABOVE Disney for a Friday start on Oct 10, so there is no saving on 2-day tickets — the only reason to use UT here is burning the Sapphire Reserve's $300 travel credit if it's unused (then it's the cheapest route by far) plus the DiningDollars.

name: Rental car — MCO (Thu–Mon) or TPA (Wed–Mon); Tesla preferred but not required

Teslas: Turo has on-site Teslas at both MCO and TPA ($182–278 trip price before Turo fees, taxes and protection plan); Hertz MCO EVs not yet priced. Gas cars via Kayak brokers run ~$26–33/day before airport taxes. If staying in Tampa with family, ask about borrowing a car first. The Friday traveler lands at MCO regardless: rideshare to Epcot (~$40–50) or pickup by the others.

options.notes: Host rating 4.93 (37 trips). $182 trip price shown 'before taxes'; Turo adds a trip fee, FL taxes and a protection plan (minimum plan is cheapest; premium adds roughly $30–60/day). Realistic all-in ~$300–400. Charging: Disney Springs and most resorts have chargers; Superchargers on I-4. Pairs with the VRBO condo that has EV charging.

Shuttle pickup, 48-hour free cancellation. Cheapest gas-car route; verify the price is per-day on the Kayak page.
